Patatas Bravas

Twice-cooked potatoes with a shattering exterior and a fluffy interior, under a smoky brava sauce that carries genuine heat. The most ordered tapa in Spain, and usually the worst made.

★★★★★★★★★★4.7(2,044)Rated 4.7 out of 5 from 2044 reviews 45 min total Serves 4 servings Easy Spanish
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

Simmering the potatoes in acidulated water before frying sets their pectin so the cubes hold their shape, while the parboil also gelatinises the surface starch into a paste that fries into a hard, glassy shell. Real brava sauce is tomato and pimentón based — not a mayonnaise — and it should be assertively hot.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Put the potato cubes in cold water with the vinegar and salt, bring to a boil, and simmer for 8 minutes until just tender at the edges but still firm at the centre.

  2. Drain and leave them in the colander to steam-dry for 15 minutes. Shake the colander to rough up the edges — those rough surfaces become the crispiest parts.

  3. For the sauce, soften the onion in the olive oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.

  4. Stir in the flour and both paprikas and the cayenne and cook 60 seconds — take care not to burn the paprika, which turns bitter instantly.

  5. Add the blended tomatoes, stock, sugar and salt and simmer for 20 minutes until thick.

  6. Blend smooth, then stir in the sherry vinegar. It should be sharp, smoky and genuinely spicy.

  7. Heat the frying oil to 190°C / 375°F and fry the potatoes in two batches for 5 to 6 minutes until deep golden and crisp.

  8. Drain on a rack and salt immediately.

  9. Pile onto a plate, spoon the warm brava sauce over the top, and serve at once with cocktail sticks.

Chef’s Tips

  • Steam-dry the parboiled potatoes properly. Wet potatoes will never crisp, however hot the oil.
  • The sauce should have real heat — "bravas" means fierce and a timid version misses the point.
  • Add a drizzle of alioli alongside, which is common in Barcelona, but keep it separate from the brava.

Pairing Suggestions

  • A cold caña of lager or a glass of vermut
  • Serve with other tapas: gambas, tortilla, olives
  • Follow with crema catalana

Storage & Reheating

The sauce keeps 5 days refrigerated and freezes 3 months. Fry the potatoes to order — they do not reheat well.
